claim: One equation, two spacings §: a plucked string sounds 1·2·3·4 and Schrödinger's box, same walls, sounds 1·4·9·16; two roads (stiffen the equation, or bump the well) meet at the squares. Latent errors the bundle's own proofs already catch: Energy Eigenvalues § calls ħω(n+½) 'identical to the harmonic series', but read as pitches the rungs are 1:3:5 (ladder-checks: 'clock = odd multiples of 110'); Hermite-Gaussian § says φ_n gives n+1 partials, which hermite-checks finds holds in none of three readings.

pieces.what: the round trip: one held tone up the stiffness road and back down the well, with the ladder ratios on screen; tests 'one substance, two knobs'
the ladder proof: rungs as pitches give odd multiples, rung differences give the harmonic series; tests the section's 'identical to the harmonic series'
pieces.walks_up_from: one rung alone, silent to the detector

pieces.what: pendulum slider: deepen the bump, hear the squares fold toward 1·2·3 and sag
